recentItems.title: How to be confident in the social media era #shorts #tedx
What is your room telling you? | Meena Krenek | TEDxAtlanta
recentItems.description:
Why can one room make you feel bold while another leaves you guarded? Design futurist Meena Krenek takes us from a childhood bedsheet fort to a high-stakes business meeting to explore the quiet influence of the spaces we enter every day. Meena Krenek has spent her career designing spaces around one conviction: Rooms don't simply hold our lives. They shape them. 

An award-winning design director, Meena creates environments that strengthen culture and forge emotional connections between people and place. For more than two decades, she has brought architecture and interior design together across workplaces, stadiums, restaurants and other spaces, using design to influence how people feel, move, connect and experience an organization.

At the heart of Meena's work is human experience. Rather than designing spaces simply to look beautiful, she considers what they communicate, how they tell a story and, ultimately, what they ask of the people who inhabit them. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Resume is Noise | Matt Baxter | TEDxMacatawa
recentItems.description:
The first recorded resume was written more than 500 years ago, and the way we hire hasn’t changed much since. HR tech veteran Matt Baxter argues that today’s hiring system buries the signal in noise for job seekers and employers alike, and he challenges both to look past the bullet points for what really matters. Matt Baxter is an entrepreneur and HR tech founder who believes the resume is noise. He started his first company, Stony Pointe Lawn Care, at 15, ran it for six years, and sold it in 2015 while studying management at Hope College.

Frustrated by the friction of frontline hiring, he wanted a faster, more human way to see who a candidate actually is. So he co-founded Wedge, an asynchronous video interviewing platform built to replace the phone screen. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Xperiment - Taylor Krause | Taylor Krause | TEDxBerkeley
recentItems.description:
A full-time content creator who many first met on Netflix’s Love Is Blind, Taylor Krause has spent nearly a decade working in climate and clean energy policy and earned a master’s degree in Energy Policy from Johns Hopkins University. But after the 2025 election defunded the long-term grant she’d been leading, she embraced a new chapter online. She now builds a lifestyle social media platform in real time, sharing authentic stories of how she is building her fulfilling life with an audience that’s growing right along with her. Taylor Krause is a full-time content creator who many first met on Netflix’s Love Is Blind, but her story reaches far beyond reality TV. Before cameras ever entered the picture, Taylor spent nearly a decade working in climate and clean energy policy, driven by a passion for meaningful, long-term impact. She earned her master’s degree in Energy Policy from Johns Hopkins University and was serving as federal policy manager at a leading think tank, where she was an expert in industrial decarbonization, particularly clean hydrogen energy.

When the 2025 election unexpectedly defunded the federal grant she had been leading for nearly three years, Taylor suddenly found herself at a major career crossroads. Supported by the community that had begun forming around her after Love Is Blind, she chose to take a leap stepping away from policy and into the digital world full-time. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Missing Page - How to Fail Without Becoming a Failure | Anshu Joshi Singh | TEDxIPEC
recentItems.description: My talk explores failure not as an identity, but as information. Through the metaphor of a book with a missing page and personal experiences of loss, rejection, change, and rebuilding, I, Anshu Joshi Singh invite the audience to rethink what failure means. The talk explores the difference between “I failed” and “I am a failure,” the importance of letting go of outdated dreams and identities, and the power of choosing what comes next. At its heart, the message is simple: we may not control what happens to us, but we retain the authorship to decide what the next chapter of our lives will be Anshu Joshi Singh is an author, life coach, author coach, NLP practitioner, motivational speaker, entrepreneur, and publishing professional who helps people navigate change with greater clarity, confidence, and self-awareness. As a life coach, she works closely with individuals on identity, relationships, motherhood, midlife, emotional well-being, and personal growth.She has authored 15 books, including her latest publications, And Then Everything Changed: How Everyday Choices Create Extraordinary Lives, Good Mother Syndrome, and Thrifty @ Fifty: Greying Greysfully. Her work reflects a strong belief that meaningful transformation begins with everyday choices. As Founder-Director of Snow Finch Publishing, Anshu also mentors aspiring authors, helping them turn ideas and lived experiences into authentic, impactful books while preserving their unique voices. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Xperiment - Jasmine Ornish | Jasmine Ornish | TEDxBerkeley
recentItems.description:
Jasmine Ornish is an independent researcher exploring the ethical frontier opened by Project CETI, a nonprofit initiative using AI and bioacoustics to study sperm whale communication. Mentored by CETI founder and marine biologist Dr. David Gruber, she created an interdisciplinary independent study and co-authored a paper examining humanity’s responsibilities if we begin to understand another species more deeply. Jasmine Ornish is an independent researcher at the intersection of artificial intelligence, interspecies communication, and ethics. Her inquiry is grounded in Project CETI, the Cetacean Translation Initiative, a nonprofit founded by marine biologist and National Geographic Explorer Dr. David Gruber. By combining machine learning with bioacoustics, linguistics, robotics, and field research, CETI is uncovering patterns in sperm whale codas previously beyond unaided human perception.

Jasmine created an interdisciplinary independent study examining the questions this work raises beyond what technology can decode. While CETI provides the scientific foundation, her contribution asks what ethical, philosophical, legal, and relational frameworks should guide humanity if technology allows us to understand another species more deeply. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Xperiment - Patrick Poole | Patrick Poole | TEDxBerkeley
recentItems.description: Patrick Poole is a research physicist at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, where he works with some of the world’s most powerful lasers to explore the behavior of matter under extreme conditions. Beyond his research, Patrick is passionate about making science accessible to everyone, from developing the next generation of fusion energy scientists to bringing scientific demonstrations to audiences of all ages. Patrick Poole is a Research Physicist at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), where he conducts plasma physics experiments at the National Ignition Facility (NIF), the world’s largest and most energetic laser system. At LLNL Patrick’s research spans high-energy-density (HED) and plasma physics, including materials science under extreme x-ray and neutron irradiation, radiography of complex hydrodynamic phenomena, photonics based on novel plasma optics, and high-average-power laser and experiment development for extreme ultraviolet lithography. Patrick also serves as Workforce and Outreach Lead for the Livermore Institute of Fusion Technology, developing the future fusion energy workforce; Coordinator of LLNL experiments at the Laboratory for Laser Energetics, supporting fundamental science and NIF campaigns; and Director of the NIF and Photon Science Summer Scholar Program, bringing hundreds of students annually to conduct cutting-edge research alongside LLNL scientists. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Conversations That Could Change Us | Cecilia Puente | TEDxMacatawa
recentItems.description:
Before we speak, most of us quietly calculate what’s safe to say, and when we do speak, we argue to win. Cecilia Puente makes the case that conversations that matter ask us to take three risks: being heard, being wrong, and being changed. Drawing on the ancient Greek idea of parrhesia, she shows how courage, curiosity, and openness can turn disagreement into discovery. Cecilia Puente is a high school junior, writer, and youth leader interested in how we communicate across differences. She has shared her writing and ideas through essays, competitions, and public forums. Through programs at Georgetown, Harvard, and the University of Chicago, she has studied courageous discourse, public speaking, debate, and approaches to building connected communities. She has carried these experiences into national youth boards and civic leadership initiatives, and is creating opportunities for dialogue in her community.

Cecilia also mentors younger students and studied ballet for over a decade. She is particularly interested in dialogue and polarization. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: When Intelligence Becomes Artificial, What Makes Us Human? | Nina Shaye | TEDxMacatawa
recentItems.description:
What if the most dangerous thing you can give a child is an immediate answer? After losing her aunt to pancreatic cancer, student researcher Nina Shaye taught herself machine learning to build an AI model that detects early-stage tumors, and learned what AI can’t do. She makes the case that purpose, choice, and wonder are what make us human in an age of instant answers. Nina Shaye is a junior at the Kalamazoo Area Math and Science Center and Portage Central High School. Passionate about both STEM and the arts, she conducts research in machine learning and cancer detection and has presented her work at international research conferences, including the International Science and Engineering Fair and International Youth Research Conference.

Nina is also an accomplished visual artist, having won the Congressional Art Competition and received multiple Scholastic Gold Keys. She is deeply involved in the West Michigan community and founded Ladybug Art Camp, which introduces young girls in Kalamazoo to the fundamentals of visual arts. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Los derechos que la vida me negó | Eufrosina Cruz | TEDxUJED
recentItems.description:
¿Qué sucede cuando el lugar donde naces, tu origen y las costumbres de tu comunidad parecen determinar lo que puedes o no puedes llegar a ser? Eufrosina Cruz comparte la historia de una niña indígena zapoteca a quien la vida le negó oportunidades desde el principio: crecer en un entorno donde las mujeres estaban destinadas a servir, obedecer y convertirse en madres desde muy pequeñas. Pero también es la historia de alguien que decidió cuestionar aquello que parecía normal y dejar de aceptar que su origen definiera su destino.
A través de sus experiencias, reflexiona sobre el poder de la educación, la palabra y las pequeñas decisiones que permiten desafiar las desigualdades. Desde aprender a cuestionar su entorno hasta abrirse camino en espacios donde le dijeron que no podía estar, su historia nos invita a reconocer que la costumbre no justifica la violencia ni la injusticia, y que los derechos no deberían depender del lugar donde nacemos. Porque cambiar una historia también significa cuestionar el sistema que hizo que tantas otras personas no pudieran cambiar la suya.
 Activista y política mexicana de origen zapoteca, reconocida por su defensa de los derechos de las mujeres y los pueblos indígenas. En 2007 inició una lucha por los derechos políticos de las mujeres, desafiando las costumbres que le negaban el interés de participar en las elecciones de su comunidad por ser mujer, una experiencia que marcaría el rumbo de su trayectoria.

Es Contadora Pública por la Universidad Autónoma Benito Juárez de Oaxaca y Maestra en Ciencia Política por la UPAEP. Fue la primera mujer en presidir el Congreso de Oaxaca y, como diputada federal, impulsó reformas para garantizar los derechos políticos de las mujeres indígenas y combatir los matrimonios infantiles y forzados.

Reconocida por Forbes entre las mujeres más poderosas de México, es autora de Los sueños de la niña de la montaña y continúa trabajando por los derechos de las mujeres, los pueblos indígenas y la niñez. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: I Feel, Therefore I Am | Leonor Varela | TEDxFrutillar
recentItems.description:
What if feeling our deepest emotions is the key to reconnecting with ourselves and with life?
In this deeply personal TEDx Talk, actress Leonor Varela explores emotional awareness, vulnerability, grief, and the courage it takes to feel what we fear most.
Through the loss of her son Matteo, Leonor discovers that avoiding emotional pain can disconnect us from ourselves, while allowing ourselves to feel can open the door to self-love, healing, and a deeper experience of human connection.
A reflection on grief and loss, emotional healing, the mind-body connection, and what it means to be truly alive. Sometimes, the place we fear entering is where love is still waiting for us. Leonor Varela is an internationally recognized actress and dedicated activist. She is also a prominent Chilean cultural figure and mother. Varela is the author of the memoir, "Ir al cielo y Volver" (Go to Heaven and Back), sharing her profound personal journey. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Cybernetics and You! | Drew Morgan | TEDxMacatawa
recentItems.description: From cruise control to kidneys to the Federal Reserve, every stable system runs on the same hidden architecture: cybernetics. Drew Morgan breaks down four core concepts (feedback, feed forward, lag, and saturation) and shows how to use them to build steadier systems at work and in life. Drew is a Park Township based engineer, maker, and sometimes artist who has also lived in the South and on the other (salty) West coast. He enjoys the intersection of the profound with the absurd. He strives for delightful form and satisfying function in everything he does, especially when it’s unexpected. He spends his time working for Disher Engineering in Zeeland, pursuing curiosity, tinkering, and exploring West Michigan with his wife and two daughters. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
